newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index dragged down by SAP fall.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index dragged down by SAP fall.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares was dragged down on Wednesday by German high-flyer business software firm SAP AG, which plummeted after the company issued a profits warning.
SAP preference shares listed on the DAX index tumbled over 23 percent and single-handedly pushed the whole index into negative territory.
The DAX index fell 20.77 points, or 0.76 percent, to 2,698.21, although the index had been slightly firmer rising to 2,725.73 in early trade, before SAP shares started floor dealings.
SAP preference shares dived 64.90 marks, or 23.4 percent, to 212.50 marks, after the group stunned markets on Tuesday evening with an unexpectedly sharp slowdown in growth in the third quarter.
The third quarter figures forced SAP to revise down its 1996 revenue forecast to 3.5 billion marks from the 3.8 billion marks previously expected.

Dietmar Hopp, chief executive of the company which had been the darling of the DAX index, said the market's reaction to the firm's profit warning was exaggerated and and said a cut in the dividend was "unthinkable".
Although most attention was centered on SAP, dealers said there would be some interest in the banking sector ahead of the nine-month reports of certain banks.
"If there is disappointment in those results, then the market could really suffer," said one dealer.
Deutsche Bank is due to publish nine-month results on Thursday, followed by Bayerische Vereinsbank on Friday.
"People are trying to buy now, because we're mostly expecting good profits," said one trader.
